headline: Kakao reports content-adaptive video latents with sparse-position generation
summary: Kakao's KATok paper reports a video VAE that learns per-token keep/drop masks and uses a cascaded mask prior to place sparse latents during generation. On about 5,000 Panda-70M validation clips, the authors report 366 average 64-channel tokens with 31.24 PSNR and 5.12 rFVD at 256²×16; at 512²×32 they report 1,554 tokens, 33.23 PSNR and 6.40 rFVD. For UCF-101 generation with the same SiT-XL backbone, cascaded position conditioning reports gFVD 61.53 versus 100.00 for Omni-VAE. The results are paper-reported; token counts alone overstate compression because KATok uses 64 latent channels versus 8 for the listed baselines.
